events.region: South Slopes of the Western Brooks Range; Noatak Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and
18 inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Red Dog Mine and the South Slopes of the Western Brooks
Range.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Mostly rain is expected below 800 feet. The
heaviest precipitation is expected Tuesday and Wednesday. Some rain
is possible near Red Dog Mine Tuesday. The heaviest snow is
expected Wednesday. Temperatures cool Wednesday into Thursday.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend. 1-3 more inches of precipitation
are expected by the end of the week which will keep water levels
high.

No flooding is expected at this time, however residents living near
local rivers and streams should be vigilant of the potential for ice
in culverts and other stream passage structures to restrict flow
resulting water flowing over roads in affected areas.
